API changelog#

Every change to the ingest API, the viewer's URL knobs and the embed SDK, newest first, exactly as recorded when it shipped. The current contract is the API reference; this page is the history behind it. Entries since 2026-08-20 are dated by the sprint window they shipped in (DevLog #7: S1 = 22–24 Aug, S2 = 24 Aug → 5 Sep, S3 = after 5 Sep); exact commit dates are not recorded here.

  • 2026-10-25 — Pricing v2 (frozen plans), branch pricing-v2. Plans are Free / Starter / Pro / Scale / Enterprise; Studio, Verse for Real Estate, All Access and the $79 Pro are grandfathered (not sold; POST /v1/billing/checkout answers 400 for them). Every allowance is enforced with 402 upgrade_required, now always carrying error, limit, used, plan and upgrade_url (plus a nudge); new gated allowances storageGB, bandwidthGB, apiCallsPerMonth, filmsPerMonth (video exports), capturesPerMonth, rendersPerMonth (still exports). API calls (any Authorization: Bearer request except /v1/plans, sign-in and webhooks) are counted per account and key; near the limit responses carry Verse-Upgrade. Allowances reset on the subscription's billing date. POST /v1/billing/checkout takes code (a discount code); new POST /v1/billing/pack {pack} (broker packs), GET /v1/coupons/check?code=, POST /v1/coupons/attribute, GET /v1/nudges, POST /v1/nudges/event, GET /n/<id>. GET /v1/account/plan gains meters, apiKeys, packs, bandwidth, offer; GET /v1/plans gains allowances, payg, packs, trialOffer, seatPlans (the apiUsage views block is gone). GET /v1/brand may carry throttle: true (owner over bandwidth: the viewer renders lighter). See Plan allowances.
  • 2026-10-25 — Release 5: capture to link (feature #1, branch feat-capture). POST /v1/ingest (one-shot or resumable) accepts a phone video of a room (MP4 / MOV / WebM / AVI, recognised by container magic) or a zip of 20–300 room photos (no model inside), or anything with X-Verse-Kind: capture / begin kind: "capture"; it becomes a splat scene (.vsp, v2 under VERSE_VSP_V2=1) plus ingest/<id>.stage.json (walk view at eye height, a tour along the filmed path). While it runs the record's stage is capturing with capture: {stage: frames|poses|training|cleanup, progress, …}; the done record carries path: "capture" and capture: {source, frames, placed, splats, timings, attempts, floor}. New error codes capture_too_short, capture_too_few_photos, capture_too_blurry, capture_no_poses, capture_no_floor, capture_empty, capture_unreadable, capture_heic, capture_unavailable, capture_failed. WhatsApp: a video (or a video document) starts a capture and the link comes back (VERSE_WA_CAPTURES_PER_DAY, default 2).
  • 2026-10-25 — Release 5: default camera paths, interactivity, packages. GET /v1/scenes/<id>/paths gains auto: {id, kind, edited}; each path gains kind (walk / drone / orbit) and auto. New GET · POST /v1/scenes/<id>/paths/auto ("Reset to auto", owner; 422 when there is nothing to plan from); ?autoplay=path and the embed option autoplayPath / attribute autoplay-path. New GET · PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/interact (hotspots, interactive objects, toggles; 64 KB). Telemetry act rows gain cta and object. The npm packages are published as @ctruhtech/verse-sdk, @ctruhtech/verse-viewer, @ctruhtech/verse-react, @ctruhtech/verse-vue (the earlier @verse/* names were never published). See Camera paths, Interactivity.
  • 2026-10-24 — Release 4: web games, sign-in, billing guard, Spatial Bench. New game routes POST /v1/games, …/replace, PATCH /v1/games/<id>, PUT …/cover, POST …/share, DELETE, GET /v1/account/games and X-Verse-Kind: game on ingest (Web games); games are served from the separate origin play.ctruh.io. Sign-in by code adds the browser-only /v1/auth/* routes (options, code, verify, me, link, sessions, signout-everywhere); tokens keep working for the API. Billing: POST /v1/billing/checkout answers the same URL while a checkout under 15 minutes old is open (reused) or 409 checkout_pending with it; /v1/billing/cancel and DELETE /v1/billing/checkout clear it. Camera paths (/v1/scenes/<id>/paths, /paths/<pid>) are owner-written and mirror scene visibility on read. Spatial Bench adds public /v1/bench/* routes behind the /bench page (run ticket, results, share card, leaderboard); they are not part of the stable API.
  • 2026-10-24 — Release 3: uploads. A glTF packed in a zip (scene.gltf + .bin + textures) is packed into one GLB on the server; STL (binary and ASCII) is accepted; new error code zip_invalid (a zip without a model or missing its .bin). KHR_node_visibility is applied and dangling animation channels are dropped, with the result saying what was left out. No route changes.
  • 2026-10-24 — splat streaming at world scale (feature #7, branch feat-splatstream). .vsp v2 (hierarchical LOD, 16-byte records, progressive SH) opens with the same ?model=x.vsp link on both tiers (tier C included; v1 stays tier A/B). Mixed scenes: ?model=<capture>.vsp&vpk2=<mesh>.vpk@x,y,z adds streamed meshes to a v2 capture, ?vpk=<scene>.vpk&splats=<capture>.vsp@x,y,z adds a v2 capture to a mesh scene (same-origin only); meshes and splats depth-compose. QA knobs ?knobs=splatpool<records>,splatbudget<splats>,splattau<px×10>,splattarget<ms>,splatnosh. Server: VERSE_VSP_V2=1 makes the splat ingest route pack v2 (unset = v1, as before); .vsp v2 files sign with the same VSPS trailer over their own head. Worker messages: splat-ready/splat-progress gain version: 2 and lod stats; new splat-added.
  • 2026-10-20 — upload limits + automatic preparation. No fixed 512 MB wall: POST /v1/ingest/begin accepts a raw size up to the plan's rawUploadMB (Free 2 GB, Pro 10 GB, Studio 20 GB, All Access 20 GB, Enterprise custom via VERSE_MAX_RAW_MB); the plan's existing size limit now applies to the prepared size. Job records gain prepare (state running/done/choice, line, tiers, choice) and convert.textureWarning; new POST /v1/ingest/<job>/choice; GET /v1/limits gains oneShotMaxMB, resumableAboveMB, preparedLimitMB and maxUploadMB is the Free raw cap. New error code prepared_too_large.
  • 2026-10-16 — 4.0.0. /v1/config and /v1/health/deep report version: "4.0.0"; nothing existing changes shape. Floor plan to 3D home: POST /v1/plan2home/analyze, POST /v1/plan2home/build (followed like an upload through GET /v1/ingest/<job>), GET /v1/plan2home/status — both POSTs use the upload's rate, key and quota gates (Floor plan to 3D home). Tour together: POST /v1/tour/invite → a short /t/<code> link (GET /v1/tour/invite/<code>, GET /t/<code> → 302 into the room as a guest; memory only, 24 h, VERSE_TOUR_INVITE_TTL_H / VERSE_TOUR_INVITES_PER_HOUR), POST /v1/room/<room>/leave (the pagehide beacon), room signals ping / end and the host flag, a 5 s stream heartbeat (Tour together, live). Analytics: GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics[.csv], GET /v1/account/analytics[.csv], GET|PUT|DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/enquiry; telemetry adds view / act rows and batches look samples (one POST per ~10 s) under its own 3600/hour bucket. Viewer report: GET /v1/scenes/<id>/report[.csv], revocable report links GET|POST /v1/scenes/<id>/report/links + DELETE …/report/links/<linkId>, read by GET /v1/reports/<token>[.csv] and the page /r/<token> (Analytics). Embeds: an oEmbed provider GET /oembed?url=<share link> (CORS *, 1200/hour), discovery + Open Graph tags on share pages, the lazy poster-first card GET /embed; embed options guard and fullscreen; embed.js, /sdk/verse-viewer.js and /sdk/verse-sdk.js are served with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin (oEmbed). Upload from a URL: POST /v1/ingest/url {url, name?, kind?, bake?, path?, look?, scan?} → the same 202 {job}, public addresses only, at most 3 re-vetted redirects, same size cap; 400 url_blocked, 502/504 url_fetch_failed (Upload from URL). Scan import: X-Verse-Scan: clean | off (or scan on begin) forces or skips the scan cleanup, X-Verse-Up and X-Verse-Units set a capture's up axis and unit (on the resumable path: the headers on commit, or up / units on begin), X-Verse-Kind: ply for a PLY mesh, .xyz / .pts text clouds and tour export bundles are accepted, records carry scan / frame, and GET /v1/limits publishes scanImport (POST /v1/ingest, Import a scan). Compile fleet: a worker that claims with X-Verse-Caps: bake is offered "Bake for me" parts (kind: "bake-part", posted back to …/result) before compile jobs (Compile fleet). SDK (@verse/sdk 4.0.0): uploadFromUrl() / publishFromUrl(), scenes.analytics() / analyticsCsv(), accountAnalytics() / accountAnalyticsCsv(); new packages @verse/viewer (<verse-viewer>), @verse/react, @verse/vue — built, not yet on npm. Limits unchanged: 512 MB per upload (2 GB prepared), 45 min per job, 30 min per attempt, 6 uploads/hour/IP anonymous, 20/hour with a token.
  • 2026-10-12 — 3.0.0-beta.1 (public beta; includes 2.7.2 and 2.8). Fidelity mode: X-Verse-Path: fidelity | streamed on POST /v1/ingest (and the resumable begin) publishes a textured product or scan as itself (ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb, opened by /view?glb=); every job record carries classification (what the shared classifier would pick) and, for a Fidelity upload, glbUrl, digest, signature. X-Verse-Look: studio:neutral|warm|dark[,bg:rrggbb] sets the look a link opens with (?look=). New owner routes GET · PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/background and PUT …/background/image; ?bg= on any link wins; embed setBackground / getBackground and the background event. The upload card's lighting is a three-way Lighting choice (keep as exported · bake preview · bake final) — X-Verse-Bake is unchanged. Scene bytes from a bucket-backed server are proxied through the origin with the same range/ETag/cache contract instead of a 302 to the bucket (VERSE_S3_REDIRECT=1 restores the redirect). /v1/health/deep adds checks.storage on a bucket-backed server. Details: API reference, Fidelity mode.
  • 2026-10-10 — 2.7.0: media surfaces + spatial audio. New routes (media.mjs): GET /v1/scenes/<id>/media (public, mirrors the scene's visibility, no-store; 204 when none) → {scene, media:[{material, url, loop, emissive, audio}], audio:[{pos, url, radius, loop, gain}]}; PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/media (owner; ≤ 4 surfaces, ≤ 16 emitters, same-origin URLs; the table is written into the scene's staging manifest and follows it through versions; 409 for a scene without a manifest); POST /v1/scenes/<id>/media/upload (owner; one raw file, container-sniffed — mp4 / webm video ≤ 200 MB, mp3 / m4a / ogg / wav / webm audio ≤ 20 MB → {path, url, bytes, kind, ext}, stored as ingest/<id>.media/<n>.<ext> under the scene's visibility, Range-capable, deleted with the scene). The staging manifest gains optional media / audio keys (viewers must read them through the GET route, not the immutable static copy). SDK: scenes.media(), scenes.setMedia(), scenes.uploadMedia(). Embed SDK: setMedia(table | null), getMedia(), setAudioMuted(muted); events media and audio. Viewer knobs: ?media=0 (do not mount the table), ?motion=reduce|full (override prefers-reduced-motion: one poster frame vs playback). Nothing existing changes shape.
  • 2026-10-10 — 2.6.0: @verse/sdk and the route table. No wire change. New: the typed, dependency-free JS/TS client @verse/sdk (sdk/, docs/sdk.md) covering every public route — VerseClient with one-shot and resumable upload (progress, cancel, prepared), waitForJob with stage callbacks, scenes/share tokens/versions/diffs/review/heatmap/publishing/presence/operations, the upload-fail beacon with telemetry: false, and embedViewer() over embed.js; served at /sdk/verse-sdk.js (+ .d.ts, embed-types.d.ts, embed-variants.html) with embed.js's headers. The Postman collection is now generated from scripts/api-routes.mjs (50 requests; adds limits, contact, current, versions, heatmap, assistant, leads) and scripts/api-parity.mjs gates server ⇔ table ⇔ api.md ⇔ sdk.md ⇔ SDK drift (web/test/fix-verify-sdk.mjs). Documented, not changed (backlog BL-67…70): no CORS on /v1/*/static files (browser SDK is same-origin only), no per-scene GET, version promotion lagging done, .d.ts MIME. The v0 /verse-sdk.js stays served for existing pages; the quickstart's stale status: "failed" is corrected to "error".
  • 2026-10-01 — 2.1.0: upload experience. New: GET /v1/limits (public; enforced limits, labelled recommendations, live queue and timing), POST /v1/ingest/<job>/contact (name, phone, email + consent → an email when the scene is live), GET /v1/ops/leads (operator-only). Job records gain attempt, healing, progress, etaS, etaText, queue, preflight, fixes, contact, attempts, stats.healed and — on failure — errorInfo { code, title, message, fix, retryable }. Behaviour changes a client can notice: (1) a job's error is still a string but is now a friendly sentence with its fix, not the compiler's message — do not pattern-match it, use errorInfo.code; (2) files the server cannot build (not a GLB, external references, no meshes, unsupported required compression, truncated) fail at the first poll instead of after a compile attempt; (3) a GLB that lists a look-only extension (KHR_texture_transform, KHR_materials_*) as required now builds instead of failing; (4) the stages textures (fast mode) / textures (safe mode) are gone — retries report textures with attempt/healing — and signing is new; (5) estimateS is calibrated from recent builds when the server has history; (6) error bodies on the ingest routes carry errorInfo next to error. (7) verify before done: a scene is checked (integrity hash, signature, counts, bounds, texture streams, staging) before done; records gain verify and stats.mode, and the stages verifying / publishing are new; (8) lossless fallback: a job whose every build attempt fails now ends done with stats.mode: "classic", a ?model=ingest/<id>.classic.glb url, modelUrl (no vpkUrl), fallback and notice — clients that require vpkUrl on done must handle its absence; (9) restarts: resumable upload sessions and finished job records survive server restarts, commit is idempotent, GET /v1/ingest/part/<id> reports job once committed. HTTP statuses, X-Verse-Error, the 202 {job} shape and every existing field are unchanged.
  • 2026-10-01 — Verse Engine 2.0.0. First production release; the wire protocol below is unchanged by the version bump. See CHANGELOG.md for the full engineering changelog and docs/releases/2.0.0.md in the repository for the user-facing notes.
  • 2026-09-30 — WC-6 client review pins reach the embed SDK. The "click a spot, leave a note" workflow is no longer playground-only: Verse.embed(el, { review: true }) (or data-review="1") runs the same review.js machinery inside the iframe, with viewer.setReviewMode(on) to toggle it, viewer.getComments() to read the current list, and verse:event names "review-posted" / "review-selected" ({id, pos, text}) for the SDK's .on(). Private-scene embeds pass their existing share token (new share embed option, also required for scene/vpk/model on a private scene — a pre-existing gap this closes) straight through to the review routes, same gate as the scene bytes; anonymous visitors of an unlisted/public scene just comment with an optional name, same as the playground. Owner moderation (resolve/delete) stays playground/studio-only by design — embeds never fetch the owner-cookie check and never render those buttons. The composer clamps to the iframe's own bounds and scrolls internally, so it fits down to a 320px-wide embed. review.js's core already took an explicit context object rather than playground globals; this ships the embedded + onEvent hooks that let embed-host.js drive it without reaching into playground DOM. See embed-sdk.md and the parity table.
  • 2026-09-30 — Dedicated 4K hero texture pool. The compiler already encoded the top VERSE_HERO_TEXTURES materials (default 12, source-gated ≥ VERSE_HERO_DIM, default 4096) at full 4096² resolution, but the runtime had nowhere to put them: every streamed blob landed in the single 2048² pool, so a hero blob was transcoded from mip 1 and its screen texel was always a 2048 resample. A second, dedicated array — tier A only, 8 slots @4096² BC7 (≤96 MB, gpu.rs TIER_A_HERO_POOL_SLOTS/TIER_A_HERO_POOL_MAX_BYTES) — now takes any upload that actually lands at ≥4096², so the handful of hero surfaces stream at full resolution and can never evict an ordinary 2048 resident. No new region-table column: vg.wgsl's per-material params.y slot index is shared between the two pools ([1, 100) = base slot, [100, ∞) = hero slot, HERO_SLOT_ENCODE_BASE in gpu.rs), and both arrays are sampled unconditionally with select() picking the real one (same implicit-derivative rule the atlas/pool split already followed). decode-worker.js requests the blob's full source resolution (maxDim=4096) for base-color fetches only when engine.tier (a getter, not a method) is "A" and the QA tier-B override isn't set; a non-hero blob is already ≤2048 natively so this is a no-op ceiling for it, not a target size. Tier B (and the ?ssrb=1 QA override, which now also disables the hero pool — there is no other way to force tier-B behavior on a real tier-A GPU) keeps the exact old mip-1-downsample path into the base pool, unchanged. Diagnostics: vg_hero_pool_stats() → [format, slots, slot_width_px, resident_count, charged_bytes_lo, charged_bytes_hi], forwarded to the playground as window.__vgHeroPool and a · hero N/8×4096px status-bar suffix when non-empty. QA: web/test/fix-verify-heropool.mjs compiles a synthetic 4096² checkerboard fixture, confirms the vpk's hero-sized blobs, and screenshots a close-up before/after — the hero pool must raise a center-crop Laplacian-variance sharpness metric over the same view with the pool forced off.
  • 2026-09-30 — "Publish to Verse" for Unity ships. integrations/unity/com.ctruh.verse-publish — a proper UPM package (Unity 2021.3+, com.unity.cloud.gltfast dependency) with a Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish Scene editor window mirroring the Blender add-on's UX: scene name (defaults to the active scene) or selection-only export, server URL + account token in EditorPrefs (token in a password field), progress from export → upload % (file-streamed UploadHandlerFile, HTTP/1.1) → the server's live compile stage passed through verbatim → done, cancel at any phase, result link with copy/open, verbatim app errors, one retry on transient/edge failures only (the X-Verse-Error contract), 30-minute total budget, polling on EditorApplication.update so the editor never blocks. The protocol layer (VersePublishClient.cs) is UnityEngine-free plain C#; web/test/fix-verify-unity.mjs replays its exact request shapes against a live local server and validates layout + the make_tarball.sh UPM tarball. Written against the glTFast 6.x export API; first in-editor run remains QA-6.
  • 2026-09-26 — S14 HDR display output. Viewer knob ?hdr=auto|1|0 (default auto): on HDR-capable displays ((dynamic-range: high)) a tier-A adapter configures the swapchain as rgba16float with extended tone mapping, so highlights past SDR white — hot speculars, emissives with intensity > 1 — drive real display headroom instead of clipping. ?hdrpeak=<linear peak> (default 2.0, clamped [1, 8]) caps the headroom. The SDR range renders identically (goldens/fidelity are byte-stable, both run SDR); ?hdr=1 forces the float16 surface anywhere (headless tone-maps it back down), ?hdr=0 pins SDR, and a runtime display change applies on the next GPU recovery or reload. QA truth: stats fields hdr + surfaceFormat, hook window.__verseHdr, harness web/test/fix-verify-hdr.mjs.
  • 2026-09-25 — API ergonomics: error contract, per-token rate limits, resumable uploads. Four fixes surfaced by the Blender add-on work. (1) Error contract: every origin-generated error response now carries X-Verse-Error: 1 and a JSON {"error": "…"} body — an error without the header came from the edge/proxy, not the app (see the error contract). (2) The ingest job stage vocabulary is documented (see GET /v1/ingest/<job>). (3) Per-token ingest rate limit: requests with a valid account Bearer token draw from their own bucket (default 20/hour/token, VERSE_INGEST_PER_HOUR_TOKEN) instead of the per-IP bucket (default 6/hour, now VERSE_INGEST_PER_HOUR-tunable) — shared NATs stop starving authenticated exporters. (4) Resumable uploads: POST /v1/ingest/begin {size, name} → {uploadId}, ordered PUT /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId> with Content-Range (out-of-order = 409 carrying the server's received offset), POST /v1/ingest/commit/<uploadId> → the same 202 {job} as the one-shot path, which is untouched. Stale uploads sweep after 2 h. The Blender add-on uses the resumable flow automatically for files over 100 MB.
  • 2026-09-25 — WC-6 Client review mode: pinned comments on shared scenes. Any shared scene link becomes a review workflow: the viewer grows a "💬 Review" chip once a served ingest scene is up — a client clicks a spot (the FEAT-10 GPU pick), types a note, and the comment is pinned to that 3D position; every comment renders as a numbered DOM pin projected from world to screen, faded with distance, working in orbit and walk mode alike. New routes: POST /v1/review/<sceneId> {pos, text ≤500, author? ≤40} → {id, t} (rate-limited per IP, 200 comments/scene cap), GET /v1/review/<sceneId> → {comments} (private scenes need the owner's auth or a share token — the same gate as the scene bytes), DELETE /v1/review/<sceneId>/<id> and POST /v1/review/<sceneId>/<id>/resolve (owner-only; resolved pins grey out and hide behind a toggle). Storage is a per-scene append-only JSONL under the dotfile dir ingest/.reviews/ — never served, dies with its scene on delete/eviction. GET /v1/account/scenes entries gain reviews: {open, total}. See Review comments.
  • 2026-09-23 — WC-5 Export video: tour → MP4/WebM, client-side. The playground viewer grows an "⬇ Export video" chip beside the ▶ Tour chip on any scene with a tour (compile-time .stage.json staging or a ?tour= replay): it records the tour flythrough from the live canvas — canvas.captureStream(0) + MediaRecorder, frames requested on a fixed timeline at the chosen fps — and downloads <scene>-tour.mp4 (H.264, where the browser muxes MP4; Chrome/Edge 126+, Safari) or .webm (VP9 elsewhere), the chip labeled with the real container. Options: duration (tour length default), 1080p/720p/native. During capture DRS is pinned to scale 1, demand-mode parking is blocked, and the render target runs at the output resolution; everything restores after (cancel restores too). Zero server cost — nothing is uploaded. Scripting/QA: window.__verseExportVideo({duration, fps, height, format, bitrate, download}) resolves the Blob.
  • 2026-09-20 — Private scenes & share tokens (WC-4 follow-up). Each owned scene carries visibility: "public" | "unlisted" | "private" (PATCH /v1/scenes/<id> {visibility}, owner-only; unlisted is the default and today's exact behavior; public is reserved for a future gallery and serves like unlisted). A private scene's artifacts — the .vpk/.vsp plus .stage.json, .plan.svg and poster — require the owner's auth or a share token: POST /v1/scenes/<id>/share mints one (32 hex, shown once, stored hashed), ?share=<token> or X-Verse-Share grants read access, DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/share/<shareId> revokes. Strangers see plain 404s (existence never advertised) with an X-Verse-Private: 1 header so the app can say "This scene is private." Private scenes bypass the CDN (VERSE_CDN_BASE): they always serve from the origin, never 302. Anonymous/unowned scenes are untouched. See Visibility & share tokens.
  • 2026-09-20 — WC-4 accounts, Studio & per-scene analytics. POST /v1/account {name} creates a token-only account (the 64-hex token is shown ONCE and is the credential — treat it like an API key); POST /v1/account/login {token} sets the httpOnly verse_session cookie so /studio — the new scene-library dashboard — works in a browser. Ingests, posters, tours and experiences sent with account auth (Authorization: Bearer <token> or the cookie) are stamped with an owner; POST /v1/scenes/<id>/claim takes an unowned scene, DELETE /v1/scenes/<id> removes an owned one, and GET /v1/account/scenes, GET /v1/scenes/<id>/stats, GET /v1/account/stats roll up opens / unique sessions / minutes viewed from telemetry (client batches now carry scene). Accounts sit BESIDE the API-key quota mode — anonymous uploads and every existing share link behave exactly as before. See Accounts & Studio.
  • 2026-09-14 — S9 closes the "not yet" list. FEAT-37: additive scenes' walk grids join the walkable set at their placements (translation + yaw; scaled placements sit out) — multi-building experiences walk end to end. FEAT-38: setMaterial({index, baseColor}) now also tints STREAMED scenes (per-material albedo multiplier in the VG shader; pick → material index → tint; resetMaterials() clears both paths).
  • 2026-09-14 — S9: multi-scene authoring, posters, SDK tours. FEAT-34: the ?edit=1 editor's Scenes section authors multi-scene experiences — add streamed .vpk objects at x/y/z/yaw/scale offsets with immediate additive preview; publishing emits scenes: [{url, position, yaw, scale}] with the base as entry 0 (single-scene drafts keep the plain scene spelling; removing a scene re-previews on reload, like props). FEAT-35: 📸 Poster captures the live viewport in the render worker and POST /v1/poster (PNG, ≤ 4 MB, magic-checked) publishes it as ingest/poster-<id>.png — ready-made for the embed's data-poster. FEAT-36 SDK tour parity: viewer.load("….tour.json") loads the tour's scene and replays the camera path exactly like the playground's ?tour=; a tour {name, seconds} event fires at playback start and stopTour() hands input back.
  • 2026-09-14 — S8: scale placement + recorded tours. FEAT-31: streamed-object placement gains uniform scale — scenes: [{url, position, yaw, scale}], knob url@x,y,z*yaw*scale; the refinement cut is scale-invariant by construction (error and camera distance share object units), and framing bounds now come back placed. FEAT-33 recorded tours: the editor's ⏺ Record tour samples the camera at 10 Hz and POST /v1/tour publishes {name, scene, samples} → a ?tour=ingest/tour-<id>.tour.json link that loads the scene and loops the camera along the path (all viewer input paused while touring).
  • 2026-09-13 — S7: shared tours, splat ingest, yaw placement. FEAT-29 live tours: joinRoom({room, name}) / leaveRoom() / follow(id) + presence events (SSE + tiny pose POSTs at /v1/room/<id>/{events,pose}; viewers render as in-world avatars; playground ?room=name&as=Me with a viewers panel and minimap dots; poses are memory-only, 10 s TTL). FEAT-28 splat ingest: POST a .ply/.splat capture to /v1/ingest (X-Verse-Kind: splat, or sniffed) → streamed .vsp share link with stats:{splats, chunks}. S7 placement: multi-scene entries and ?vpk2= take a yaw — scenes: [{url, position, yaw}], knob url@x,y,z*yawDeg; lighting, picking and shading stay world-correct under the rotation.
  • 2026-09-14 — FEAT-32 signed .vsp + CDN parity: captures verify like scans. Packed .vsp splat captures now carry the same Ed25519 signature as compiled .vpk scans — as a pure 80-byte trailer ("VSPS" + version + payload_len u64 + 64-byte signature over SHA-256(header ‖ chunk table); the 32-byte .vsp header has no reserved bytes for a descriptor — docs/vpk-format.md §8). The ingest server signs after splat-pack succeeds and splat job records gain signed: true|false; boot-signing covers unsigned ingest/*.vsp from before this date. The browser verifies from the head it already fetched plus one Range request for the trailer (GET /v1/pubkey, WebCrypto) and reports signed: true | false | "unverified" (playground vsp-signed message, window.__verseVspSigned, " · signed" on the status line) — a missing or bad signature never blocks streaming. CDN offload reaches parity too: with VERSE_CDN_BASE set, GET ingest/*.vsp answers 302 like .vpk (same VERSE_CDN_RANGES rules, same X-Verse-CDN-Pull pull-through escape) and finished splat records carry cdnUrl.
  • 2026-09-14 — FEAT-28 splat ingest: capture → streamed .vsp share link. POST /v1/ingest accepts Gaussian-splat captures (.splat antimatter15 or INRIA 3DGS binary .ply): send X-Verse-Kind: splat (or let the server sniff — ply\n magic, or a 32-byte-aligned body with neither the VPK1 nor the glTF magic) and the job packs a streamed .vsp via splat-pack instead of compiling a mesh — same 512 MB limit, quotas, rate limits, job polling and stage reporting (packing). The finished record carries url (?model=ingest/<id>.vsp), vspUrl and stats: {splats, chunks}; .vsp files are served from ingest/ but not Ed25519-signed (signing is .vpk-specific), and splat jobs always pack on the origin (the INF-4 fleet runs verse-compile only). The playground upload flow takes .ply/.splat too: ≤ 16 MB loads whole in the browser as before, larger captures ingest and stream. (The "not signed" part was superseded the same day by FEAT-32 above: .vsp files are now signed.)
  • 2026-09-14 — FEAT-27 Gaussian-splat streaming (FEAT-12 v2). Multi-million-splat captures stream by chunk from a new .vsp v1 container (packed offline by verse-compile's splat-pack binary: splat-pack input.splat|input.ply -o out.vsp — header + 32 B/chunk table + per-chunk 48 B records with the coarse subset as a payload prefix, so one byte range serves either LOD). The runtime opens on the head, then a 150 ms residency tick range-fetches the [chunk, level] plan a projected-size cut wants (Full above ~64 px, Coarse while visible, None beyond 1.3× the viewing sphere), into a slab-pooled splat buffer capped at 2M resident records — farthest chunks demote Full→Coarse, then evict, under pressure. Depth sorting runs over the resident set only. Playground: ?model=x.vsp or drop a .vsp; status live-counts "N / M splats · streaming". Whole-file .splat/.ply loading (FEAT-12 v1) is unchanged. Tier A/B only; tier C reports "Gaussian splats need WebGPU". No ingest-server splat pipeline yet — .vsp files are packed offline and served as static ranged files.
  • 2026-09-13 — FEAT-26 multi-scene streaming. Several .vpk objects stream in one frame: the renderer holds N virtualized-geometry objects, each with its own pipelines, pools, residency loop and a world translation baked into a per-object globals copy (shaders and the refinement cut stay object-space). Picks answer across all objects (nearest hit wins); stats aggregate (vgPerObject per object). Experience manifests: scenes: [{url, position}] — first entry keeps the camera and walk grid. Playground: ?vpk2=url@x,y,z;…. Whole-file load_vpk, GPU-recovery restreaming, and signatures all carry over per object.
  • 2026-09-13 — S5 viewer features. setSun(azimuth, elevation, intensity) (time-of-day: shading + shadows move together; ?sun=az,el,int); setMaterial({index, baseColor, metallic, roughness, emissive}) / resetMaterials() (live finish variants on classic scenes, both tiers; ?material=idx:rrggbb;…); measure tool (playground key M, two taps → metres; streamed scenes — picking is GPU-side); floor-plan minimap from the walk-collision grid (auto in walk mode, key N, ?minimap=1; shows viewer dot + heading and experience hotspots).
  • 2026-09-12 — FEAT-19 XR controllers + teleport (v1); hardware pass pending QA-5. In-headset locomotion drives the SAME sim-side collision walk as the desktop controls: left thumbstick walks (deadzone 0.15), right thumbstick X snap-turns ±30° per flick (hysteresis latch), trigger — or a thumb-index pinch with hand tracking — teleports along the controller ray onto the floor plane (8 m clamp, landing eye 1.6 m up, level gaze). The XR reference space rides a walker "rig" composed into the stereo eye matrices, so walking/turning/teleporting moves the viewer while the headset keeps 6DoF. Walk mode turns on for the session and restores after. No teleport arc/aim visual yet; input→message mapping is unit-tested without hardware (web/test/xr-input.test.mjs).
  • 2026-09-12 — FEAT-20 Unreal exporter completed (code). tools/verselink-unreal now performs the whole flow: automated glTF export via Epic's exporter, POST + 202 {job} polling with the same resilience rules as the Unity/Blender paths, clipboard + open-in-browser on success, per-project endpoint config ([VerseLink] Endpoint in EditorPerProjectUserSettings). Still never compiled against an editor — the first Unity/Unreal editor runs remain QA-6.
  • 2026-09-12 — INF-4 compile fleet (origin side). Set VERSE_WORKER_TOKEN and external workers (tools/verse-worker) pull compile jobs over /v1/work/* (claim → source/images → stage → result, Bearer-authenticated); the origin signs delivered files and records workedBy. No claim in 10 s, a claim silent for 20 min, or a worker-failed report → the in-process compiler takes the job, so zero workers is exactly the previous behavior.
  • 2026-09-12 — INF-5 telemetry forwarding · FEAT-16 CDN offload · INF-6 boot-signing. VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL (+ optional VERSE_TELEMETRY_AUTH bearer) batch-forwards telemetry lines as application/x-ndjson every 15 s (≤500 KB/batch, 5 MB retry queue, local JSONL unchanged as fallback); VERSE_CDN_BASE (+ VERSE_CDN_RANGES=0 opt-out for ranged requests) makes GET ingest/*.vpk answer 302 to the CDN and adds cdnUrl to finished job records; at startup the server signs any .vpk on the volume whose signature descriptor is zero (pre-INF-6 files), logging "boot-signed N of M .vpk files". See docs/telemetry.md and docs/handover/devops.md.
  • 2026-09-12 — INF-7 tier-C diet shipped. The WebGL2 bundle no longer contains wgpu: a raw web-sys WebGL2 renderer (one program, GL state for the four pipeline variants) with the shader translated from WGSL at build time by the same naga version. 3.70 MB → 1.28 MB raw, 901 KB → 345 KB brotli. Pixel-identical to the previous backend (goldens pass unchanged); all suite checks pass. simulate_device_loss now loses the real GL context on tier C.
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-21 experience editor (v1). ?edit=1 opens an authoring panel over the loaded scene: capture the current view as the walk spawn or a named hotspot, tap a surface to place a GLB prop / particle emitter / positioned sound (via the FEAT-10 pick), tune depth of field — everything previews live through the same messages the runtime replays. Download the .verse.json, or POST /v1/experience (≤128 KB JSON, scene required) stores it as ingest/exp-<id>.verse.json and returns {path, url} — a share link. ?edit=1&experience=<url> loads an existing manifest for editing. Not in v1: gizmos, material overrides, removing placed items from the live preview.
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-17 docs site at /docs. GET /docs/ serves a no-build documentation site from the same server (web/playground/docs/): the repo's Markdown rendered in the browser (GET /docs/<name>.md, whitelisted names under docs/, docs/handover/, docs/patents/), sidebar + on-page outline + heading search, dark/light, mobile layout, and a Live examples page that embeds the real product through embed.js (streamed 30 M-triangle scene, animated GLB, experience manifest with goTo() hotspots, Gaussian splats) with copyable snippets. New pages docs/getting-started.md and docs/embed-sdk.md (generated from verse-embed.d.ts). The playground header links to it.
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-15 inspector: ?inspector=1 / key I. Playground devtools panel: budget meters per memory category (memory_breakdown() export, both tiers), streaming residency heat-map per DAG level (vg_level_histogram(), vg_summary(); empty on tier C), scene tree (scene_summary() rides the scene message; vpk-ready carries summary), 120-frame CPU/GPU sparkline (per-frame samples batched on the 2 Hz stats message). QA hook window.__verseInspector. See the runbook's Inspector section.
  • 2026-09-11 — INF-6 signed .vpk. Every compiled .vpk is signed Ed25519 by the ingest server (SHA-256 over the header with the signature slot zeroed + the whole directory, so the per-group checksums are covered; 64-byte trailer, descriptor in header bytes 104–119 — docs/vpk-format.md §8). New GET /v1/pubkey → { alg: "Ed25519", spki }. The browser verifies with WebCrypto (no wasm cost) and reports signed: true | false | "unverified" through a signed embed event that follows loaded once the directory has paged in (verse-embed.d.ts), and on the playground status line (" · signed"). A missing or bad signature never blocks loading — files compiled before this date are simply unsigned. Job records gain signed: true|false. Server key: VERSE_SIGNING_KEY (base64 PKCS8 DER) or an auto-generated ingest/.verse-signing-key (see docs/handover/devops.md).
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-18 experience manifests. load("x.verse.json") composes a walkthrough: base scene (.vpk or GLB) + placed GLB props + environment + ambience + depth of field + walk spawn + hotspots (see docs/experience-format.md). Events: experience {name, props, hotspots} when parsed, loaded for the base scene, hotspot {id} on a jump; verb goTo(id). Playground: ?experience=<url> shows hotspot buttons on the stage.
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-12 Gaussian splats (v1). load(url) accepts .splat (antimatter15) and 3DGS .ply from the Verse origin; loaded carries splats: <count>. Tier A/B only: tier C emits error "Gaussian splats need WebGPU". Whole-file load, DC colour only (no view-dependent SH), CPU depth sort. Playground: ?model=x.splat or drop the file.
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-11 dynamic props. Embed SDK: spawnProp({shape, position, velocity, size, color}), throwProp({shape, size, speed, color}) (from the camera along the view), clearProps(); prop event {id, count} (id -1 = scene cannot draw props). Rigid balls/boxes collide with the scene's voxel grid, a ground plane and each other. glTF scenes only for now. Playground knob ?props=ball@x,y,z*size;box@…, key T throws.
  • 2026-09-11 — FEAT-13 particles + spatial audio. Embed SDK: addEmitter({kind, position, scale}) / clearEmitters() (GPU particles: fire, smoke, fountain, dust; tier A/B), addSound({kind|url, position, …}) / clearSounds() (Web Audio HRTF; synthesized fire/water/wind or an audio URL; starts on first gesture). Playground knobs ?particles=fire@x,y,z*scale;… and ?audio=fire@x,y,z.
  • 2026-09-11 (S3, FEAT-14) — Depth of field: ?dof=<focus m>,<aperture px·m> on the playground URL and viewer.setDepthOfField(focus, aperture) in the embed SDK (verse:dof); aperture 0 disables; tiers A/B, not applied in temporal (TSR) mode. Shipped uncommitted at the time of writing (date = this doc's date, not a commit date).
  • 2026-09-05 (S2, FEAT-8) — glTF animation: clip playback on the node hierarchy (v1), then GPU skinning + morph targets (v2; tier C renders the bind pose). The loaded embed event lists animations; control verbs play(clip), pause(), seek(t), setSpeed(speed) (verse:anim).
  • 2026-09-05 (S2, INF-2) — .vpk v5: group table moved ahead of the cluster entries with vertex/index totals, coarse-first ordering, and a paged directory (the runtime opens on a ~3.7 MB head and pages the rest of the cluster table while rendering). The reader still accepts v1–v4, so previously compiled files keep serving unchanged. (Format details are internal.)
  • 2026-09-05 (S2, FEAT-9) — Embed SDK v1 (embed.js, embed-host.js, verse-embed.d.ts): data-scene="<id>" resolves to ingest/<id>.vpk on the Verse origin (data-vpk / data-model also accepted); viewer API load, camera, walk, move, pick (promise, 5 s timeout), setEnvironment (.hdr); events ready, loaded, progress, pick, environment, view, dwell, interact, error, degraded, replayed to late listeners. The engine always runs in an iframe on the Verse origin.
  • 2026-08-24 (S1, REL-8) — ?model= (and the embed model option) is same-origin only: the host names a GLB the Verse origin serves; other origins are refused with "models load from the Verse origin only".
  • 2026-08-24 (S1, REL-7) — API keys: X-API-Key lookup is an own-property check (__proto__/constructor no longer resolve); daily usage is persisted to .verse-usage.json so a redeploy does not reset quotas; a failed compile refunds the debited MB.
  • 2026-08-24 (S1, REL-4) — Client poll hardening: the playground tolerates up to 8 consecutive failed polls (retry after 2 s) and caps at 2 700 polls (~45 min); verse-sdk.js tolerates 3 misses and honours timeoutMs (default 45 min); the server kills a compile at 30 min.
  • v2 (2026-08) — ingest is asynchronous: POST returns 202 {job} and the client polls. Added 413 (512 MB limit), per-IP rate limiting, and automatic deletion of uploaded source GLBs after compile.
  • v1 (2026-08, retired) — synchronous 200 response. Clients written against v1 must adopt the poll loop in the API reference (the bundled SDK ≥0.2 does it internally).
